gloss: taking a course; attending a lecture

definitions.gloss: taking a course; attending a lecture
definitions.explanation: The act of enrolling in and attending a course, lecture, or training program. A formal term commonly used in educational and professional training contexts.

examples.japanese: オンライン{講座|こうざ}を{受講|じゅこう}している。
examples.english: I am taking an online course.

examples.japanese: {受講|じゅこう}{申|もう}し{込|こ}みは{来週|らいしゅう}までです。
examples.english: Registration for the course is until next week.

examples.japanese: {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}は{全員|ぜんいん}、{安全|あんぜん}{研修|けんしゅう}を{受講|じゅこう}しなければならない。
examples.english: All new employees must take the safety training course.

notes:
USAGE:
{受講|じゅこう} is a formal term for attending lectures or courses. It is more formal than simply saying {授業|じゅぎょう}を{受|う}ける (to take a class) and is preferred in official contexts like university course registration or corporate training.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {受講|じゅこう}する (to take a course)
- {受講|じゅこう}{者|しゃ} (course participant, attendee)
- {受講|じゅこう}{料|りょう} (course fee)
- {受講|じゅこう}{申|もう}し{込|こ}み (course registration)
- {受講|じゅこう}{証明書|しょうめいしょ} (certificate of completion)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{聴講|ちょうこう} means to audit a course (attend without credit), while {受講|じゅこう} implies formal enrollment.
